_about: Corrections to the vendored Smithy model, for operations whose declared
success status is not the one Amazon S3 answers with. A corrected status
keeps the code checked against what S3 really returns; the alternative,
listing the operation as an accepted violation, would stop checking it.
Each correction pins the exact upstream code it replaces. If a re-vendor
changes that code, the loader fails rather than applying a correction to
a model it was never written against.

_evidence: PUT Bucket policy answers 204 No Content — the response carries no
body and S3's REST API reference documents the code. The simulator's
bucket-subresource table records the same split deliberately, because
the SDKs and `aws s3api` read it. The operation's trait declares 200,
which is the code the model assigns rather than the one S3 sends.
PUT Bucket tagging answers 204 No Content, the same way PutBucketPolicy
does and for the same reason: the response has no body. The trait
POST Object restore answers 202 Accepted when it starts a restore and
200 OK when the object is already being restored, so both are codes S3
